root_cause.text: Concurrent bitfield assignments to multiple flags (is_open, has_lease, on_list) sharing the same byte in struct cached_fid cause read-modify-write races, where updating one flag can inadvertently corrupt or restore stale values of the other flags.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Bitfield assignments generate byte read–modify–write operations... so updating one flag can restore stale values of the others. A possible interleaving is: CPU1: load old byte (has_lease=1, on_list=1) CPU2: clear both flags (store 0) CPU1: RMW store (old | IS_OPEN) -> reintroduces cleared bits." The patch then converts these flags from bitfields to separate bool fields.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove bit-field specifier from bool fields in struct cached_fid, changing them to plain bool for simplification and to avoid bit-field limitations.
intent_record.what: Changed four boolean fields in struct cached_fid from bit-field declarations (e.g., 'bool has_lease:1') to plain bool declarations (e.g., 'bool has_lease').
intent_record.how: This increases the memory footprint of the struct because each bool now occupies at least one byte instead of sharing a bitfield storage, but the runtime behavior remains semantically identical; the fields are still boolean flags.
